race: Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Welcome to Race Weekend, and Las Vegas is back under the lights, and we are ready for a huge one this weekend.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: One city, one street, one very loud weekend, and the data is already making us lean one way before practice.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Before practice starts, we are looking at past form, team pace, and what this track has rewarded before in recent years.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Quick news first, F1 is comparing Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, and the US calendar is getting proper all of a sudden.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Three US races now, and each has its own vibe, but Vegas still feels like the biggest neon spectacle of the year.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Hamilton is also pushing for more diversity in the sport, and that is a great reminder of the bigger picture for everyone.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And if you want the BBC guide for following Las Vegas, it is there, so you can settle in with a drink and a bit of noise.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Right, enough chatter, who do we trust, and why does our top ten look the way it does before the green lights?

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Our top pick is Kimi Antonelli, because Mercedes looks strong, and he has a clean record at this street under the lights.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: His best result here is third, and he has a podium from one race, which is a small sample but a confident one for the weekend.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I agree, he belongs up front, but Max Verstappen is the danger, and his Las Vegas record is the best on this circuit.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Max has a win, two podiums from three races, and strong recent form, so I would not bet against him when the track is slick.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is the man, and if Red Bull find the right balance in the night air, he is going to be hard to stop for the whole race.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Then George Russell for third, because Mercedes pace is real, and he has won here before, and it was not long ago.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: His average finish here is third point seven, with a win and two podiums, so he is not just a dark horse on these streets.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He can hurt, but I still have Kimi first, because the season story and the street feel point to Mercedes when the lights are on.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Fair, but now the deep cut, and I think Liam Lawson is the one to watch over the weekend, especially if he gets a clean run.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Racing Bulls has been consistent, and street tracks suit him, so a top ten finish feels very possible on this kind of circuit.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And Arvid Lindblad is our low confidence gamble, with points, consistency, and a few good street results in recent races.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: If the lights go green and he finds a clean lap, he can shock us, and that is the fun of Vegas when the night gets loud.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Lando Norris is fourth because McLaren has been strong, and he can be quick when the lights go on for the whole session.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Lewis Hamilton is fifth because Ferrari has strength, and his Vegas history gives him a real chance if the car is right.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Charles Leclerc is sixth because he has pace, and his Las Vegas record is solid enough to trust in the closing stages.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Isack Hadjar is seventh, Oscar Piastri is eighth, so the midfield is packed with real threats all weekend long, and they will be hungry.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Liam Lawson is ninth, and Arvid Lindblad is tenth, so the deep cut is already in the list, and it could go higher.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: If the night is fast and clean, one of those names could jump higher than we expect with a bit of luck, especially from the back.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: So here is the full top ten, and I will let Tom take one breath.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen, George Russell, Lando Norris, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Isack Hadjar, Oscar Piastri, Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad, and that is Las Vegas, see you there.
